newsitem.title: USA: Shell Oil Co oil products income slide.
newsitem.headline: Shell Oil Co oil products income slide.

text.p: Shell Oil Co, U.S. unit of Royal/Dutch Shell, said that operating income from its oil products division fell $59 million to $12 million in the first quarter of 1997.
Adjusted net income, which excludes special items, was $16 million for the first quarter of 1997, down $55 million, the company said in a statement with earnings.
"Higher feedstock and purchased product costs coupled with weak West Coast marketing conditions were the primary factors resulting in lower refined product margins," Shell Oil Co said.

It added that costs had increased in the first quarter due to scheduled refinery turnarounds and higher operating expenses, although sales of refined products rose five percent and sales of light products increased 11 percent.
Overall, the company reported a record first quarter net income of $517 million, an increase of $34 million, or seven percent, over the $483 million in the same 1996 period.
This was largely due to higher crude oil and natural gas prices.
Operating cash flow provided was $658 million for the first quarter of 1997 compared to $553 million in the 1996 period, increasing $105 million.

Oil and gas exploration and production income from ongoing operations totaled $453 million, an increase of $139 million and adjusted net income, which excludes special items, was $427 million, up $136 million from a year ago.
Domestic crude prices in the 1997 quarter rose $2.73 per barrel over the 1996 quarter to average $19.28 per barrel.
Natural gas prices rose to an average $2.93 per thousand cubic feet from $2.38, however, the company noted that prices had "declined significantly by the end of the quarter".
Domestic crude production in the first quarter rose 8,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 389,000 bpd, primarily from increased production in the deepwater Gulf of Mexico.
Natural gas production fell 138 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), or seven percent, as increased production from the deepwater was more than offset by normal declines elsewhere and property sales.
The company said that chemical products income from ongoing operations rose $20 million in the quarter to $109 and adjusted net income was up $38 million at $109 million.
Excluding special items, charges for corporate and other expenses rose $5.0 million to $53 million. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
